answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Underwritten crop insurance record with farm insurers attestation changes that arithmetic: seasons the insurers underwrote across years of farms, so the horizon for each fake is paid in the real world. The check runs before any reward is issued, so a sybil earns nothing for trying; the nadir is that the attacker discovers the price before the first coin, not after. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the signal of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
